quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise; provided that the acquiring party agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 18.9 is symmetric and gives us a full M&A/successor carve-out: either Party (including Ono) may assign without the other's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise, subject only to the acquirer's written assumption of obligations. Affiliate assignment is permitted under Section 18.9's second paragraph with the other Party's consent "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed", which sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred consent-free affiliate right; the same is true of the unqualified consent standard for other Third Party assignments and the tax-consequences proviso, but these are mutual and are minor sub-elements only. On change of control, Section 18.10 imposes only firewall obligations following a Change in Control of Array (i.e., it binds the counterparty), and no provision gives Array any right to terminate, re-price or renegotiate on a Change in Control of Ono (Section 4.5(b) likewise terminates only on Array's Change in Control). Accordingly the clause meets the fallback on all material terms and no redline is warranted.

Section 18.10 imposes only firewall obligations on a Change in Control of the counterparty (Array) and no provision gives the counterparty any termination, re-pricing or renegotiation right on our change of control, satisfying the rule's change-of-control requirement. Shortfalls versus preferred wording (consent needed for affiliate assignment, unqualified consent standard for Third Party assignments, tax-consequences proviso) are mutual and correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted in the rationale, not redlined. UNLESS EXPRESSLY PROVIDED HEREUNDER, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY OR ANY OF ITS RESPECTIVE AFFILIATES AND THEIR RESPECTIVE OFFICERS, DIRECTORS AND EMPLOYEES BE LIABLE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT

The redline removes the commencement trigger so we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice — the fallback notice period rather than the preferred 30 days, which is proportionate here given the transition mechanics in Article XIV. Noted but not separately flagged: the notice period in 13.2 is redacted and should be confirmed at 30–90 days; the wind-down/transfer costs allocated to Ono under 14.2(a) and the post-termination Competing Product restriction in Section 8.2 operate as economic consequences of an at-will exit and should be reviewed under the pricing/exclusivity rules rather than double-flagged here.

rationale: There are two audit-type rights binding us. quote: 13.1 Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13, shall continue in full force and effect, on a Product-by-Product and country-by-country basis until the Secondary Royalty Term with respect to such Product expires, at which time this Agreement shall expire in its entirety with respect to such Product in such country. Upon expiration of this Agreement, the licenses granted to Ono under Section 2.1 shall become non-exclusive, fully paid- up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights
rationale: There is no auto-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement: a document-wide search for "renew"/"automatically renew" returns only patent-term renewals and Section 14.4 (which expressly says post-expiry dealings are not a renewal or extension). The structure also favours us: on expiry Ono's licences convert to perpetual, fully paid-up, royalty-free licences, and Section 13.2 gives Ono a unilateral without-cause termination right on notice. Because none of the risks the rule targets (long non-renewal notice windows, multi-year automatic renewals, uncapped uplifts) are present, the clause satisfies the preferred position by construction and no redline is warranted.

quote: (iv) Transition. Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition in the Development, sale and ongoing marketing, promotion and commercialization of the Product in the Ono Territory during the Wind-down Period and to conduct in an expeditious manner any activities to be conducted under this Section 14.2.
rationale: A usable exit/transition regime exists and survives termination, so the rule is satisfied. Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ("Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other ... to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period"), and Article XIV in its entirety survives under Section 14.5, so the cooperation obligation runs against Array as well as us. The Wind-down Period in 14.2(a)(ii) gives a defined, bracketed transition runway keyed to the termination ground, 14.2(a)(iii) and (vi) set out orderly transfer of Regulatory Filings, Data and materials with defined outside dates (assignment consistent with Wind-down obligations; return of materials within ninety (90) days), and cost allocation is expressly addressed in 14.2(a)(i) and (iii) rather than left as an open fee exposure, which answers the planner's concern about assistance being conditioned on extra fees. This is an in-licence, not a hosted service: there is no vendor-held "Customer Data" to export, and by design the licensee holds and hands back the licensor's Product data on termination, so the preferred data-export/deletion mechanic maps only loosely onto this genre. On its material terms the clause sits at or above the fallback. ops.text: 15.4 Performance and Product Warranty. Array warrants that (a) all Development, Manufacturing, supply and other activities performed by or on behalf of Array under this Agreement will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards and in compliance with applicable Law (including, where applicable, Good Manufacturing Practices); (b) each shipment of Materials supplied by Array to Ono under Article 9 will, at the time of delivery, conform in all material respects to the applicable specifications and will have been Manufactured in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices and applicable Law, and will not be adulterated or misbranded; and (c) the Materials and any software or electronic deliverables provided by Array hereunder will not contain any virus or other malicious code. For any non-conformance with the foregoing warranties of which Ono notifies Array within ninety (90) days following delivery (or, in the case of a latent defect, within ninety (90) days after Ono's discovery thereof), Array shall, at Array's option, re-perform the affected activities, replace the non-conforming Materials or deliverable, or refund the amounts paid or payable by Ono for the same, in each case without limiting any other remedy available to Ono under this Agreement.
